title: 1637 Prairie's wing gets the engraving's wide paired upper window
items: The upper window on the front of 1637 Prairie's south wing is now the pair of sashes the engraving draws: one opening about 1.8 m across, split down the middle, where a single narrow sash stood.
Through the engraving's own camera it now covers the width the print gives it; its height already matched and is unchanged.
The print can't show how wide the bar between the two sashes is, so that width is reconstructed and listed among the liberties.
